_about: The junkyard's fights, as data (VS-17, Combat Designer; Level 1: numbers and names). Rooms and coordinates come from docs/maps/junkyard.md: metres, origin at the room's north-west floor corner, +x east, +z south. 'at' is [x, z] on the floor. Enemy ids are in data/combat/enemies.json: grunt = the Signals cop (Ross's Cyberwolf), brute = the Signals heavy, signals_drone, wall_turret. A turret entry sits in 'fixtures' (it never moves, never counts as a wave member, and is a hack target too); everything else is in 'waves'. The Level Designer's placements.json owns the hack targets (fuse boxes, crane, drone line, terminals) and the exact spawn nodes: this file says WHO shows up, HOW MANY, WHEN and WITH WHAT TUNING; the Level Designer checks the 'at' points against walls and the camera ring. Every number is a starting guess that Ross tunes by playing.

rules._about: Kingdom Hearts-style accessibility, as numbers. Fights are small, readable and forgiving: a wave never starts while the last one is still biting, new arrivals take a beat to notice, at most two enemies attack at once (enemies.json token rules), and the mix always offers a hack that makes the fight easier.
rules.respawn: A 'regular' encounter respawns when Red re-enters the room (junkyard.md). A 'sticky' one sets its clear flag for good.

battery._about: Design rule: every hack lesson comes AFTER cops have filled the battery. 'gain_est' is the battery a player would gain from the cops of the first wave at about 8 damage a Light hit and 7 battery a hit; the showcase hack costs are in hacks.json (Zap 20, EMP 40, Overclock 50). Nothing here gives battery for free.

vs_form._about: When Red is in the loader (J5, hacks off) enemy hits are scaled so the loader chips rather than dies: a cop swipe (10) lands as 6, a drone dive (7) as 4, a turret bolt (7) as 4. The loader has 480 hp (scale_profiles.json). Expected: about 35 hits over the run, so it ends the room at roughly half health.

enc_j1_pair.name: The Pound
enc_j1_pair.notes: The first fight in the game after the town. Two cops, ONE attacks at a time, 20 percent less health than the sandbox cop (38 hp: five Light hits). Both idle at the burn barrel and notice at 8 m, so Red can walk up and start the fight herself. The battery ends the fight around 100, enough for the fuse box (Zap 20) twice over.

enc_j2_chute.name: The Chute
teaches: Zap stun / EMP off / Overclock gag

hack_showcase.gag: Overclocked with nothing to shoot, it fires at the empty chute and the bark makes a joke of it

enc_j2_chute.notes: One slow turret and a 14 m lane. It fires one burst every 3 to 5 s (slower than the roster default), and the laser shows a full second before the first bolt. Three answers, all fair: strafe off the line, Zap it twice (stun 2.5 s) or EMP it (off 4 s) and walk past, or Overclock it. No enemies, so the battery is whatever Red walked in with (50 at least on a new game, plus carried).

enc_j2_pitstop.name: The Pit Stop
teaches: the turret on the ledge is yours
enc_j2_pitstop.notes: Three cops first (144 hp of sword hits fills the battery to 100). The Brute walks in about when the last cop falls, with a 900 ms warning. This Brute raises its guard 38 percent of the time (22 in the sandbox) so the player SEES the guard and the bark's EMP answer: EMP breaks it and opens it for 1.3 s. Or Overclock the ledge turret: hijacked it fires about every 1.4 s for 10 s, about 100 damage into the Brute's 220. The turret's own bursts at Red are slow and telegraphed, so a fight against all four is still readable.

enc_j3_yard.name: The Crane Yard
teaches: EMP clears drones and the guard
the drone line is a clock
enc_j3_yard.notes: The toughest fight so far, built in two beats and with a clock. Two cops, then a cop and a Brute, with the drone line trickling one drone every 6 s (never more than two alive). The EMP answer is meant to be found here: two drones plus two cops inside 4.5 m is one EMP. The line never stops by itself, so the battery can always be topped up here (no softlock). Zap its power node (two Zaps, 5 m up, lock-on target) to end it for good; EMP only pauses it for 8 s.

enc_j4_stand.name: The Stand
enc_j4_stand.notes: The hardest fight on foot. Three waves with a breather between each: three cops, then a Brute, then the second Brute with two drones. The turrets stay quiet until the cops are down (they come online with a warning bark), then fire slow bursts (one every 4 to 5 s each), so they are a dare more than a wall. The mix is a puzzle with three good answers: Overclock a turret onto a Brute, EMP the two drones and the Brute's guard together, or just beat it with the sword. A Brute enrages under 35 percent (enemies.json) and the second one will usually do it with drones in the air. No respawn: it sets j4_stand_cleared and the shutters lift. Ask the Level Designer for one small health glint just inside the shutters after wave 2.

enc_j5_lane.name: Breaker's Lane
teaches: the loader is huge, they are ants
enc_j5_lane.notes: Three ant-sized cops to show the scale. A cop has 24 hp here and a loader swing does 32: one hit each.

enc_j5_graveyard.name: Car Graveyard
enc_j5_graveyard.notes: Ten cops, six drones and two turrets, all half-health and ant-sized next to a 3.5 m loader. The loader mows them down; the point is the feel of scale, not the challenge. Cops idle in three clusters so they come in a trickle, not a wall.

enc_j5_canyon.name: Container Canyon
enc_j5_canyon.notes: Three turrets on platforms down the S-bends and an ambush of four cops and two drones. A turret bolt lands as 4 on the loader (vs_form). The canyon walls fall when hit at the base, which is the show.

enc_j5_wall.name: The Foreman's Wall
enc_j5_wall.notes: A last small group before the gate, so the climax of the run (the big gate, hp about 400) is not empty.

hack_props._about: Numbers for the junkyard's hack targets that depend on fights (the Level Designer's placements.json places them; these are the values it should use). Wall turrets and the drone line are also in the encounters above.

crane_j3.note: 10 s of Overclock and an 8 s carry leaves 2 s spare; a retry costs another 50 battery, and the drone line keeps the battery topped up.

loader_j4.note: Recommendation: interact (press the button at the cradle), not Overclock. Overclock costs 50 of battery that Red may not have after the Stand, and a story beat should never be gated by a resource.
